name: Periplasmic and Membrane Stress (Cpx Response)
description: The Cpx (conjugative pilus expression) two-component system responds to protein misfolding stress in the periplasm and inner membrane. The sensor kinase CpxA detects envelope stress signals including misfolded pili, alkaline pH, changes in membrane composition, and accumulation of misfolded periplasmic proteins. Upon activation, CpxA autophosphorylates and transfers phosphate to the response regulator CpxR, which activates transcription of >100 genes involved in protein folding, degradation, and envelope homeostasis. The Cpx response overlaps with but is distinct from the σE envelope stress response, with CpxAR primarily sensing inner membrane and periplasmic stress while σE responds to outer membrane stress. Key Cpx target genes include periplasmic proteases (DegP), protein folding factors (DsbA), and pilus assembly inhibitors. This flowchart illustrates stress detection, signal transduction through the two-component system, and the protective responses that restore envelope integrity.
scientificAccuracy: This flowchart is based on extensive genetic and biochemical studies of the Cpx system. All components (CpxA, CpxR, CpxP inhibitor), signaling mechanisms, and target genes have been well-characterized. The model represents a paradigm for bacterial envelope stress sensing and quality control in the periplasm.

notes: The Cpx system is one of several envelope stress responses in E. coli (along with σE, Bae, Rcs). The CpxP-mediated feedback regulation is elegant: CpxP both inhibits the sensor (negative feedback) and is induced by the response (amplification), with substrate sequestration of CpxP providing the switching mechanism. DegP's temperature-dependent chaperone-to-protease switch is structurally remarkable. The Cpx response is important for virulence in pathogenic E. coli as it responds to host-induced stresses. This system exemplifies how bacteria monitor protein folding quality in different cellular compartments.
